what: Franklin Electric makes pumps, motors and controls for moving water and fuel, used in wells, irrigation, homes, industry and petrol stations, and runs a distribution business that sells to contractors.
customers: Well and water-system contractors, farmers, builders, utilities and fuel retailers.
money: Pumps, motors and controls for groundwater, wastewater and water treatment
Selling water equipment to installers in the US
Pumps and equipment for petrol stations
moat: Strong brands among well contractors, a long product history and its own distribution network.
risks: Demand depends on weather, housing and farm activity
Raw-material costs such as copper and steel
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.66 billion in 2021 to $2.26 billion over the last twelve months
Return on invested capital of about 13–15%
watch: Groundwater pump volumes and margins in the distribution business.
view: Franklin Electric is a steady industrial business. Revenue grew from $1.66 billion in 2021 to $2.26 billion over the last twelve months, and net income has stayed between $147 million and $200 million. Return on invested capital has been around 13% to 15%.

The company has stepped up buybacks, spending about $166 million in 2025, and the share count has fallen slightly. At about 22 times earnings, the price is in line with other water-equipment companies, which usually trade at a premium because water infrastructure is a long-term need.

The main variable is the end market: housing starts, farm incomes and weather all affect pump demand. Analysts expect EPS to grow about 13% next year; that depends on margins recovering in the distribution segment.
bull: Water infrastructure demand and better distribution margins drive double-digit earnings growth.
bear: Weak housing and farm demand keep volumes flat and margins under pressure.
